function: Over-the-air (AirComp) aggregation for ADMM-based federated edge learning: joint design of transmit equalization, receiver beamforming, shared RIS phases and downlink beamforming to minimize aggregation MSE (p. 8).
system: One passive reflecting RIS (L = 49) serving uplink and downlink; BS with J = 5 antennas; M = 15 single-antenna devices; frequency band not stated (pp. 4, 11).
method: Federated learning with ADMM over AirComp; trained models are logistic regression and a small CNN; wireless design by classical alternating optimization, SCA, SDR (pp. 8-11).
data_channel: Own simulation: path loss exponents 3.8, 2.2, 2.2, Rician fading (factors 2, 0, 0), M = 15 devices in two regions; non-IID Fashion-MNIST and CIFAR-10 (p. 11).
test_conditions: Sweeps of communication rounds, RIS elements, BS antennas, phase bits (1 to 3) and downlink noise; average of five Monte Carlo runs; no train/test shift stated (pp. 11-13).
baselines: NR [8] (no RIS, scaling-factor equalization); RR (random RIS phases); TO (RIS, after [46]); FK (separate uplink/downlink RIS design); ER (noiseless bound) (p. 11).
metrics: Testing accuracy on Fashion-MNIST and CIFAR-10 versus rounds, RIS elements, BS antennas, phase bits and downlink noise (pp. 12-13).
complexity: Worst-case order O(tmax(J^3 + M^3 + C_DC + (J^2 + M + 1)^3)) for the AO algorithm, with the cost of each subproblem; no runtime reported (p. 11).
q1_support: p. 11: "we adopt the Rician fading channel model in this paper"; path loss exponents follow [41] and the Rician factors are 2, 0, 0. Custom simulator; no 3GPP, DeepMIMO or measured channel.
q2_support: p. 12: "The effect of the number of reflecting elements at the RIS on the testing accuracy"; p. 11: "All experimental curves presented in the paper represent the average results of five Monte Carlo simulations". Parameter sweeps with held-out test accuracy; no model trained in one setting and tested in another is reported.
q3_support: p. 11: "Scaling-factor assisted transmit equalization with DC empowered receiver beamforming design without RIS (NR) [8]" is the earlier published design; "Joint optimization with random phase shifts (RR): A RIS with random phase shifts is arranged" is the non-learned baseline; p. 12: "a noticeable performance gap remains between our design and the baseline methods".
q4_support: p. 11: "total worst-case computational complexity of Algorithm 1 is" O(tmax(J^3 + M^3 + CDC + [J^2 + M + 1]^3)), the order of the cost of the AO design.
q5_support: p. 11: "the well-known Fashion-MNIST dataset [42] and the CIFAR-10 dataset [43]" are learning-task datasets only; the channel is simulated. No code or data link is given.
notes: Included as area 7: federated learning over the air passes no_learning because the learned element is the FL model (Step 1.3), while the wireless design is classical alternating optimization (p. 10). The uplink is AirComp (p. 4: "AirComp-Based Uplink Communication"). q3 rests on NR [8], an earlier published aggregation design, and on RR, the random RIS baseline; TO is only (p. 11: "Similar to the approach in [46]") a generic RIS resource-allocation paper, and FK has no citation. Reviewer should confirm that NR [8] is an adequate earlier aggregation design. Figs. 2 to 6 were read from the page images (pp. 12, 13).
